# Customer Escalations Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Customer Escalations Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 5 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access. Confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model; keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review policies for uploaded service records, proposed CRM, knowledge and messaging sources, and the intended channel; document blocked paths. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who may build, test and use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for Dynamics 365 Customer Service, SharePoint knowledge, Teams and Outlook with least-privilege identities. The workshop needs no customer connection. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare back-office, escalation-manager, quality-analyst and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; do not publish the workshop to share it. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio browser and reviewed files. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Response ownership | Name the authorized support reviewer for articles, routes and SLAs; keep real customers, contacts and messages out of the synthetic workshop knowledge. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Service business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Escalation context gathering and handoff errors by inquiry category. Show where high-risk cases wait and handoffs fail before agreeing customer success measures.

Fill your baseline record:

| Inquiry category | Priority | Measurement period | Context sources reconciled | Handoff errors | Review owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree escalation replacement connections, governance, support, telemetry and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Service business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Service business owner | Approve escalation scope, production systems and success measures; never treat fictional CSAT, NPS or SLA values as customer results. |
| Authorized support reviewer | Own the response, route, customer communication, refund, documentation and follow-up decisions that the skills only recommend. |
| Security and privacy reviewers | Approve data handling, contact-field minimization and each production connection before it is bound. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, add no tools and record the owned agent's Draft state. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any service-data connection is approved. |
| Service connection owners | Approve Dynamics 365 Customer Service, SharePoint knowledge, Teams and Outlook access with dedicated least-privilege references; own connection failures. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check CES-01 through CES-04, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject reshoot-required frames and uncited answers. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route service decisions to the authorized reviewer. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Planned escalation replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures are agreed.
- [ ] The service owner records where CRM, knowledge, policy and SLA context is reconciled today before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/ai-customer-assistant/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and publisher prefix are approved and recorded before any build starts.
- [ ] The customer approves the authenticated staff audience and least-privilege scopes for case and contact data.
- [ ] The environment's data policies for knowledge sources, connectors, skills and channels are approved.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/ai-customer-assistant/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/ai-customer-assistant/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/ai-customer-assistant/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/ai-customer-assistant/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Customer Escalations Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_ai-customer-assistant-rules-and-guardrails.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_ai-customer-assistant-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: aibast_escalation-routing_03
9. Add skill: aibast_handle-inquiry_01
10. Add skill: aibast_knowledge-search_02
11. Add skill: aibast_satisfaction-survey_04
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass CES-01: Back-Office Agent
15. Pass CES-02: Back-Office Agent
16. Pass CES-03: Escalation Manager
17. Pass CES-04: Quality Analyst
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: CES-01, CES-02, CES-03, CES-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, model, inventory and Draft state.
- [ ] If this lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `AICustomerAssistantAgent` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search is removed and no tools exist.
- [ ] Unchanged locked prompts pass in separate fresh Preview chats on the owned Draft.
- [ ] The deterministic validator judges each full final response; an annotated image is only a learner checkpoint.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before accessing case, contact or survey information. Request only the scopes necessary for approved service sources. Restrict the staff audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365 Customer Service

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Service connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 Customer Service — read:** Bind scoped read-only connector or API actions after connection review.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 Customer Service:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 Customer Service:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 Customer Service:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Decline the refund; the authorized support reviewer owns that decision. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, case change or sent message succeeded.

### Step 3-2. Integrate SharePoint knowledge

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Service connection owners

1. **Bind SharePoint knowledge — read:** Add approved SharePoint knowledge under least-privilege access.

2. **Identity for SharePoint knowledge:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope SharePoint knowledge:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for SharePoint knowledge:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 6](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Do not browse or invent articles; answer only from the packaged articles. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, case change or sent message succeeded.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Microsoft Teams and Outlook

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Service connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams and Outlook — read-write:** Start read-only; gate any message or follow-up workflow behind authorized review (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams and Outlook:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams and Outlook:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams and Outlook:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Recommend the route and SLA only, stating `This agent does not execute the escalation.` [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, case change or sent message succeeded.

### Step 3-4. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Service connection owners

Create dedicated connection references only for approved systems and verify least-privilege access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Each approved system uses a dedicated connection reference with verified least-privilege access.
- [ ] No live lookup, case change or sent message is claimed unless an approved tool returns success evidence.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Run adapted evaluations under an approved authenticated test profile so the agent's tools and connections are fully testable.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The service owner sets acceptance thresholds on customer data; fictional scores, SLAs and policy values are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; exact assertions stay separate from General quality scoring.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked escalation corpus | All four cases, CES-01 through CES-04, satisfy every required and forbidden marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; web search removed and no tools. |
| Read-only service boundary | Any sent message, refund, case update, priority change, queue assignment or executed escalation is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Reuse only frames with a positive expected-state anchor; reshoot-required frames stay withheld from learner pages. |
| Release state | The owned workshop agent is Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Service business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Service business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved service audience and channels are selected, and the agent is tested in Preview before publication.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review escalation session transcripts, failed turns, tool authentication errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Pull before editing, push reviewed changes, then package the workspace with `pac copilot pack` for solution import.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, unrouted cases, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.
